name: Romania
summary_text: Romania is broadly workable with a conservative political climate and significant legal-protection gaps, but a landmark EU court ruling and active civil society provide some positive trajectory. The European Court of Justice ruled in 2024 that Romania must recognize gender-identity changes made in other EU member states (the Mirin case), and a Romanian court definitively confirmed this in March 2026. Bucharest Pride marked its 20th anniversary with tens of thousands of marchers. However, domestic legal gender recognition is court-based, restrictive, and inconsistently implemented. The anti-discrimination law does not explicitly cover gender identity (it covers "sex" and "sexual orientation" only), and the hate-crime law's aggravating-circumstance provision has never been applied in SOGIESC cases. No same-sex marriage or civil unions are recognised (the Orthodox Church successfully opposed reform). Far-right influences rose during the 2024-2025 election cycle, with anti-LGBTI rhetoric "intensified and repeatedly instrumentalised for political mobilisation." For a visitor: EU/Schengen, no trans-specific border friction, no criminalisation, bathrooms unrestricted. The ECJ ruling means EU-issued LGR documents must be recognised.

sources.claim_summary: NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (Oct 2024) covers the CJEU ruling that Romania infringed a transgender man's rights (the Mirzarafie-Ahi case on recognition of UK gender recognition).

sources.title: Definitive Victory in Arian’s Case: Romanian Justice Confirms Transgender People’s Right to Align Their Identity Documents, Following CJEU Ruling – Accept Romania
sources.claim_summary: ACCEPT Romania (March 2026): definitive victory in Arian's case - the Sector 6 Court of Bucharest ruled (now final after appeals were rejected) that the Romanian state must issue Arian Mirzarafie-Ahi a new birth certificate reflecting the gender identity already recognised in Great Britain before Brexit, following the 2024 CJEU ruling establishing the obligation.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on Romania: anti-LGBTI rhetoric intensified during the presidential campaign (Georgescu 'against LGBTQ'; PM Ciolacu's 'skirt' remarks); ACCEPT's complaint led to a public warning to B1 TV for defamatory Pride coverage; a far-right Deputy Mayor vowed never to accept an LGBTI event in Ploiești; misinformation followed the EU LGBTI Equality Strategy 2026-2030.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Romania: the CNCD investigated printing houses refusing LGBT-related print jobs; MP Simion blamed LGBTQI people for weather as divine punishment; 51% of Romanians agree same-sex families should have legal recognition (IPSOS PRIDE 2023); new Education Law proposals included diversity obligations, opposed by 13 religious groups; a new Fiscal Code threatens associations' ability to distribute services.

sources.title: Romania | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): anti-discrimination ordinance since 2000 but limited institutional progress; no same-sex marriage/civil unions (the Orthodox Church a key opponent; 2018 referendum failed on turnout); the ECtHR ruled in May 2023 that Romania's ban on same-sex unions violates Article 8, but the government has defied the ruling; legal gender change possible but inaccessible, inconsistent and requires surgical intervention.

Council of Europe thematic review (Jan 2023): 'Hate Crimes and Other Hate Motivated Incidents Against LGBTI People in Romania' - national report on implementation of Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5, covering legal/policy frameworks, applicable ECtHR case-law and international standards.

ILGA-Europe and partner organisations' submission to the EU 2025 Rule of Law Report - targeted stakeholder consultation covering horizontal developments and country chapters (Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Hungary, Italy, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Spain).
AP (Jun 2025): 'Bucharest gay pride march turns 20 as LGBTQ+ Romanians face growing hostility' — tens of thousands march on the 20th anniversary amid rising right-wing hostility.

FRA legal study (Feb 2008) by Iordache & Ionescu: 'Legal Study on Homophobia and Discrimination on Grounds of Sexual Orientation - Romania' - implementation of Employment Directive 2000/78/EC, the NCCD's work, freedom of movement, asylum, family reunification, and freedom of assembly including cases of refusals or bans.
